title: Zalameda urges CA to act on Maguindanao massacre appeals
summary: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to promptly resolve the pending appeals in the Maguindanao massacre case, as the country marked the 17th anniversary of the…

blocks.text: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to promptly resolve the pending appeals in the Maguindanao massacre case, as the country marked the 17th anniversary of the tragedy.

Speaking at his first flag-raising ceremony as Chief Justice, Zalameda said the victims and their families had waited long enough for justice, stressing that the proceedings should no longer be delayed.

“As we speak of protecting those who stand for justice, we must also remember the victims of the Ampatuan Massacre, whose 17th anniversary we commemorate today. The victims and their families have waited long enough,” Zalameda said.

“I therefore urge the Court of Appeals to resolve the pending appeals with dispatch, consistent with due process and rights of all parties. Let us ensure that justice is not delayed any further,” he added.

The Maguindanao massacre, also known as the Ampatuan massacre, took place on Nov. 23, 2009, when a convoy carrying relatives and supporters of then Buluan Vice Mayor Esmael Mangudadatu, along with journalists and other civilians, was ambushed in Ampatuan town, Maguindanao.

The victims were accompanying Mangudadatu’s wife, Genalyn, and other family members as they were on their way to file his certificate of candidacy for the 2010 gubernatorial elections. Fifty-seven people were killed in the attack, including 32 journalists and media workers, making it the deadliest single attack on journalists in history.
The family of photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay, whose remains were never recovered, continues to seek his recognition as the 58th victim of the massacre.— MCG, GMA News
